column1: Reading another transaction's uncommitted changes is a {{c1::dirty read}}.
column2:
The other transaction can later roll back the change you read.
Review source

column1: Within a transaction, rereading a row and seeing another transaction's committed change is a {{c1::nonrepeatable read}}.
column2:
The reading transaction did not make the intervening change itself.
Review source

column1: Within a transaction, a repeated query returning extra matching rows inserted by another transaction shows {{c1::phantom reads}}.
column2:
The search condition is the same, but the matching row set changes.
Review source

column1: SQL Server's default session isolation level is {{c1::READ COMMITTED}}.
column2:
Database configuration determines whether its reads use shared data locks or row versions.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Database, READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT defaults to {{c1::ON}}.
column2:
The usual starting configuration is READ COMMITTED with RCSI and optimized locking.
Review source

column1: Enable SNAPSHOT transactions in StudyDB with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE StudyDB SET ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION ON;}}
column2:
Enabling the database option does not automatically select SNAPSHOT for a session.
Review source

column1: Before starting a SNAPSHOT transaction, select the session level with {{c1::SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SNAPSHOT;}}
column2:
The database must also have ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION enabled.
Review source

column1: Enable RCSI for StudyDB with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE StudyDB SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON;}}
column2:
Other connections must be closed while changing this database option.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Database, optimized locking is {{c1::always enabled}}.
column2:
It combines transaction ID locking with lock after qualification when RCSI is enabled.
Review source

column1: Optimized locking depends on the recovery feature {{c1::accelerated database recovery (ADR)}}.
column2:
ADR is already enabled in Azure SQL Database.
Review source

column1: Under optimized locking at READ COMMITTED, an exclusive {{c1::transaction ID (TID)}} lock protects modifications until transaction end.
column2:
Fewer long-held row/page locks reduce lock memory and escalation risk.
Review source

column1: Reserve one unit only when available: UPDATE dbo.Products SET StockCount = StockCount - 1 WHERE ProductID = @ProductID AND {{c1::StockCount > 0}};
column2:
Assume ProductID is unique and StockCount starts nonnegative. Check the affected-row count before creating the order in the same transaction.
